content.value_statement: LLM teams need visibility into traces, cost, latency, quality, and prompt changes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through practical Langfuse instrumentation and evaluation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to initialize Langfuse clients for cloud or self-hosted deployments.
Shows how to create traces, generations, scores, metadata, tags, users, and sessions.
Covers automatic OpenAI SDK tracing, including streaming and async examples.
Demonstrates LangChain callback integration for chains, agents, and retrievers.
Identifies common observability anti-patterns such as missing flush calls and noisy traces.
Summarizes limitations for self-hosting, high-volume workloads, dashboard latency, and evaluations.
limitations: Requires an existing Langfuse account or self-hosted Langfuse instance.
Does not provision infrastructure, dashboards, alerts, or production secrets.
Examples focus on Python integrations and do not cover every SDK option.
Evaluation guidance is introductory and still requires domain-specific scoring design.

use_cases.title: Instrument a Chat Application
use_cases.description: Add traces, generations, user identifiers, session identifiers, and token usage to an LLM chat workflow.

use_cases.title: Monitor Production Quality
use_cases.description: Use scores, tags, metadata, and sessions to investigate latency, cost, user feedback, and prompt regressions.

use_cases.title: Trace Agent Frameworks
use_cases.description: Connect Langfuse callbacks to LangChain chains, agents, and retrievers for end-to-end observability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Basic Tracing
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new LLM application
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Langfuse skill to outline the minimum tracing setup for my chat application. Include traces, generations, user identifiers, session identifiers, usage, and flush behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Instrumentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned Langfuse instrumentation for missing trace fields, weak metadata, noisy spans, and serverless flush risks. Give practical corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Design Evaluation Signals
prompt_templates.scenario: Add quality measurement to production traces
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Langfuse scoring approach for customer support conversations. Include feedback scores, automated quality signals, tags, metadata, and dataset usage.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Framework Observability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced tracing across chains, agents, and model calls
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Langfuse observability architecture for a LangChain agent system with OpenAI calls, retrievers, streaming, async execution, prompt versions, and regression tracking.

output_examples.input: I need to add observability to a support chatbot.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend creating a trace per user request, logging each model generation, attaching user and session identifiers, recording token usage, adding support-specific metadata, and flushing before serverless exits.

output_examples.input: Our LangChain agent is hard to debug in production.
output_examples.output: The skill would suggest a Langfuse callback handler, meaningful trace and span names, agent-level metadata, callback configuration for chains and tools, and focused tags for production investigations.

output_examples.input: We want to compare prompt versions safely.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose prompt version tracking, feedback and evaluation scores, datasets for regression checks, cost and latency monitoring, and tags that separate experiments from production traffic.

best_practices: Use stable user and session identifiers so traces can be grouped and debugged.
Log only useful spans, metadata, tags, and scores to keep observability data searchable.
Flush traces at the end of serverless or short-lived jobs to prevent data loss.
anti_patterns: Do not trace every internal step when it creates noise without diagnostic value.
Do not omit user and session context from production traces.
Do not rely on dashboards alone without scores, datasets, or feedback loops.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you instrument LLM applications with Langfuse tracing, scoring, prompt tracking, and framework callbacks.

faq.question: Does it work with OpenAI applications?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes OpenAI SDK tracing patterns, including standard calls, streaming, and async usage.

faq.question: Does it support LangChain?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to use the Langfuse callback handler with chains, agents, retrievers, and default callback configuration.

faq.question: Can it deploy Langfuse for me?
faq.answer: No. It assumes you already have Langfuse Cloud or a self-hosted Langfuse instance available.

faq.question: Can it design evaluations?
faq.answer: It can help plan scores, datasets, and feedback collection, but final evaluation criteria depend on your product and users.

faq.question: Is it only for production systems?
faq.answer: No. It is useful during development, staging, and production when you need trace history and prompt comparison.
